lines.t: Conversation 1.
lines.cn: 对话一。

lines.t: F: Mr.
lines.cn: F：大卫·杰克逊先生，

lines.t: F: David Jackson, a staff writer at The New Yorker, is known for his non-fiction books of adventure.
lines.cn: F：《纽约客》的专职撰稿人，以其非虚构冒险题材的作品闻名。

lines.t: F: Today we go on a different kind of adventure, Jackson's life of parenting his offspring.
lines.cn: F：今天我们谈的是一种不同的冒险——杰克逊养育子女的生活。

lines.t: F: David, as a parent of an 11 and a 14-year-old, what is the most interesting issue you are dealing with right now?
lines.cn: F：大卫，作为 11 岁和 14 岁孩子的父亲，你现在正处理的最有意思的问题是什么？

lines.t: M: It's easy to focus on the challenges, but so far I find these ages to be kind of wonderful.
lines.cn: M：人们很容易关注挑战，但到目前为止，我觉得这个年龄段其实挺美好的。

lines.t: M: They are independent and they have their own curiosities and obsessions.
lines.cn: M：他们独立，有自己的好奇心和执迷的事。

lines.t: M: You can talk to them about fairly sophisticated subject matter such as politics.
lines.cn: M：你能和他们谈相当复杂的话题，比如政治。

lines.t: F: Yes, that does sound refreshing compared with talking to younger children.
lines.cn: F：是的，跟和更小的孩子说话相比，这确实让人耳目一新。

lines.t: F: Do they ask you to proofread their essays?
lines.cn: F：他们会请你帮他们校对作文吗？

lines.t: M: Certainly, with writing they do.
lines.cn: M：写作方面当然会。

lines.t: M: I really just try to be encouraging.
lines.cn: M：我其实只是尽量鼓励他们。

lines.t: M: I think at this age editorial guidance is less important than encouragement.
lines.cn: M：我觉得这个年纪，编辑上的指导不如鼓励重要。

lines.t: F: Are there books that you think are important that your children read and that all children read?
lines.cn: F：有没有一些你认为很重要的书，你的孩子读了、所有孩子也都该读？

lines.t: M: My general thought is to read widely and to incorporate a love for reading.
lines.cn: M：我的总体想法是广泛阅读，并把对阅读的热爱融入其中。

lines.t: M: Learning to love to read, I think, is the optimal thing because it gives you a skill you can take anywhere.
lines.cn: M：我认为学会热爱阅读是最理想的，因为它给你一种走到哪里都能用得上的本领。

lines.t: F: So you're not too concerned, like some parents, with the content they're reading?
lines.cn: F：所以你不像有些父母那样，太在意他们读的内容？

lines.t: M: I know I have some worries about that.
lines.cn: M：我知道我也有点担心这方面。

lines.t: M: Yeah, read what you like.
lines.cn: M：不过，读你喜欢的就好。

lines.t: M: If a child loves graphic novels or comic books, whatever it is that is turning them on to read and turning on their imagination.
lines.cn: M：只要孩子爱上图像小说或漫画书，无论是哪种，只要能让他们爱上阅读、激发他们的想象。

lines.t: F: I feel that children's tastes in books change as they reach adolescence.
lines.cn: F：我觉得孩子对书的品味会随着进入青春期而改变。

lines.t: F: I know that mine certainly did when I was a teenager.
lines.cn: F：我知道我十几岁时就是这样。

lines.t: F: What do you think?
lines.cn: F：你觉得呢？

lines.t: M: I think it's especially important as they get older to read subject matter that will open their eyes to the world and people.
lines.cn: M：我觉得随着年龄增长，读那些能让他们看清世界与世人的题材尤其重要。

lines.t: M: So I think both fiction and non-fiction are really important because they give you the power to begin to perceive the world through the lives of others.
lines.cn: M：所以我认为虚构和非虚构都很重要，因为它们赋予你一种能力，让你开始通过他人的生活去感知这个世界。

tasks.title: Sec A · 第 2 组

questions.stem: What do we learn about the woman?

options.A: She is a website designer.

lines.t: Conversation 2.
lines.cn: 对话二。

lines.t: M: In this episode of Money Talks, our guest is Molly Sanders, a university student and a successful young entrepreneur.
lines.cn: M：本期《谈钱》的嘉宾是莫莉·桑德斯，一名大学生，也是一位成功的年轻创业者。

lines.t: M: Molly, tell us about your business.
lines.cn: M：莫莉，讲讲你的生意吧。

lines.t: F: Well, I sell specialty clothes through a website, mainly for women who have trouble finding suitable clothes in main street shops because of their height or weight.
lines.cn: F：好，我通过网站销售特型服装，主要面向那些因为身高或体重，在高街商店里买不到合适衣服的女性。

lines.t: F: But I do some men's clothes too.
lines.cn: F：不过我也做一些男装。

lines.t: M: How did you get started in this business at such a young age?
lines.cn: M：你这么年轻，是怎么做起这门生意的？

lines.t: M: Are you studying fashion design?
lines.cn: M：你学的是服装设计吗？

lines.t: F: Actually, I'm majoring in finance, but I've always loved clothes, and I started making my own at 14.
lines.cn: F：其实我主修金融，但我一直喜欢衣服，14 岁就开始自己做衣服。

lines.t: M: Did you have any sort of training in design or sewing, or was it a natural ability?
lines.cn: M：你在设计或缝纫方面受过什么训练吗，还是天生就会？

lines.t: F: I'd have to say no to both.
lines.cn: F：两样都得说没有。

lines.t: F: No one taught me to make clothes, and most of the things I made at first were disasters.
lines.cn: F：没人教我做衣服，而且我最初做出来的大部分都是灾难。

lines.t: M: Why did you persevere?
lines.cn: M：那你为什么坚持下来了？

lines.t: M: I think most people would give up if they kept failing, especially at that age.
lines.cn: M：我觉得大多数人如果一直失败，就会放弃，尤其是那个年纪。

lines.t: F: I kept on out of necessity.
lines.cn: F：我是迫不得已才坚持下来的。

lines.t: F: As you can see, I'm very tall, and I couldn't find clothes that fit me in ordinary shops, so I kept trying and developed my skills over time.
lines.cn: F：你看得出来，我个子很高，在普通商店里买不到合身的衣服，所以我不断尝试，慢慢练出了手艺。

lines.t: M: Well, my notes say you earned $50,000 in profits last year, an extraordinary amount for a 20-year-old student.
lines.cn: M：嗯，我的记录说你去年的利润是 5 万美元，对一个 20 岁的学生来说是笔惊人的数目。

lines.t: M: How did that happen?
lines.cn: M：这是怎么做到的？

lines.t: M: Did you see a gap in the market and decide to fill it?
lines.cn: M：是你发现了市场空白，决定去填补它吗？

lines.t: F: No.
lines.cn: F：不是。

lines.t: F: When I started university, some classmates complimented my clothes, and when I said I made them myself, other tall women started asking if I would make theirs.
lines.cn: F：我上大学时，一些同学夸我的衣服好看，我说是自己做的，于是其他高个子女生开始问我能不能也给她们做。

lines.t: F: And I did, and before I knew it, I was an entrepreneur.
lines.cn: F：我就做了，不知不觉中，我就成了创业者。

lines.t: M: So what are your plans for the future?
lines.cn: M：那你未来有什么计划？

lines.t: M: Do you intend to open a physical store?
lines.cn: M：打算开实体店吗？

lines.t: F: No, I'll keep things online to keep costs down, but I will add more clothes for children, both girls and boys, and possibly even for infants, and I hope to add to my range of designs for men.
lines.cn: F：不，我会继续做线上以压低成本，但我会增加更多童装，男孩女孩的都有，也许还会做婴儿装，另外我希望扩展男装的设计系列。

options.B: Discovering bacteria which are resistant to all known antibiotics.
options.C: Identifying bacterial strains that are most harmful to human health.
options.D: Removing a deadly strain of bacteria in humans with a new antibiotic.

questions.cn: 研究者做出了什么史上首次的事？

optionsCn.A: 利用人工智能发现一种强效新抗生素。
optionsCn.B: 发现对所有已知抗生素耐药的细菌。
optionsCn.C: 识别对人类健康危害最大的菌株。
optionsCn.D: 用新抗生素清除人体内的致命菌株。

options.A: Ever-increasing strains of bacteria.
options.B: Bacteria's resistance to antibiotics.
options.C: The similarity between known drugs.
options.D: The growing threat of bacteria to health.

questions.cn: 为什么寻找新型抗生素药物很重要？

optionsCn.B: 细菌对抗生素的耐药性。
optionsCn.C: 已知药物之间的相似性。
optionsCn.D: 细菌对健康日益增长的威胁。

options.A: Dispense with experimental testing.
options.B: Predict whether compounds are toxic.
options.C: Foresee human reaction to antibiotics.
options.D: Combat bacteria's resistance to antibiotics.

questions.cn: 文章说人工智能在抗生素研究中能做到什么？

optionsCn.C: 预见人类对抗生素的反应。
optionsCn.D: 对抗细菌的耐药性。

lines.t: Passage 1.
lines.cn: 短文一。

lines.t: Researchers have identified a potent new antibiotic compound using artificial intelligence.
lines.cn: 研究者利用人工智能发现了一种强效的新型抗生素化合物。

lines.t: The antibiotic can kill very dangerous bacteria.
lines.cn: 这种抗生素能杀死非常危险的细菌。

lines.t: According to a study published in the journal Cell, the compound successfully removed deadly strains of bacteria in mice, which are resistant to all known antibiotics.
lines.cn: 根据发表在《细胞》期刊上的一项研究，该化合物成功清除了小鼠体内对所有已知抗生素都具有耐药性的致命菌株。

lines.t: The researchers say this is the first time that artificial intelligence has been used to find a powerful new antibiotic molecule.
lines.cn: 研究者说，这是人工智能首次被用于发现一种强效的新型抗生素分子。

lines.t: Why does this matter?
lines.cn: 这为什么重要？

lines.t: The answer is antibiotic resistance.
lines.cn: 答案是抗生素耐药性。

lines.t: This happens when bacteria develop the ability to survive the medications designed to kill them.
lines.cn: 当细菌发展出在被设计来杀死它们的药物下存活的能力时，就会出现这种情况。

lines.t: Antibiotic resistance is a serious threat to health.
lines.cn: 抗生素耐药性是对健康的严重威胁。

lines.t: And the problem is growing.
lines.cn: 而且这个问题正在加剧。

lines.t: This makes finding new antibiotics very important.
lines.cn: 这使得寻找新型抗生素非常重要。

lines.t: However, in recent decades, very few have been developed.
lines.cn: 然而近几十年来，新开发的抗生素极少。

lines.t: And those that have tend to be very similar to drugs already available.
lines.cn: 而且已开发出来的那些往往与现有药物非常相似。

lines.t: These searches also tend to only focus on a narrow spectrum of chemical compounds.
lines.cn: 这类搜寻也往往只聚焦于一个很窄的化合物范围。

lines.t: But this is where artificial intelligence comes in.
lines.cn: 而这正是人工智能发挥作用的地方。

lines.t: Why?
lines.cn: 为什么？

lines.t: To find new drugs, scientists screen molecules to predict how effective they might be.
lines.cn: 为寻找新药，科学家筛选分子，以预测它们可能有多有效。

lines.t: Typically, such screening is done by humans in the lab, which is both costly and slow.
lines.cn: 通常这种筛选由人在实验室里完成，既昂贵又缓慢。

lines.t: Artificial intelligence is different.
lines.cn: 人工智能则不同。

lines.t: It's fast and it can process a high volume.
lines.cn: 它速度快，还能处理海量数据。

lines.t: It can screen hundreds of millions of compounds to identify a few interesting candidates that require experimental testing.
lines.cn: 它能筛选数亿种化合物，找出少数值得实验测试的有趣候选者。

lines.t: Artificial intelligence is also able to predict if compounds are likely to be toxic.
lines.cn: 人工智能还能预测化合物是否可能有毒。

lines.t: Some experts assert that this work signifies a paradigm shift in antibiotic discovery.
lines.cn: 一些专家断言，这项工作标志着抗生素发现的一次范式转变。

lines.t: It could change drug discovery more generally.
lines.cn: 它可能更广泛地改变药物发现的方式。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: According to the passage, how do most people detect lying?

options.A: By theorization.
options.B: By generalization.
options.C: By observation.
options.D: By conversation.

questions.cn: 根据文章，大多数人如何识别谎言？

optionsCn.C: 通过观察。
optionsCn.D: 通过交谈。

questions.stem: What does the passage say about most lies?

options.A: They are easy to detect.
options.B: They are well intended.
options.C: They are groundless.
options.D: They are harmless.

questions.cn: 关于大多数谎言，文章说了什么？

optionsCn.C: 它们毫无根据。
optionsCn.D: 它们是无害的。

questions.stem: What have many studies uncovered about the average person's lie detection?

options.A: Mostly by chance.
options.B: Basically objective.
options.C: Subject to their mental alertness.
options.D: Dependent on their analytical ability.

questions.cn: 许多研究发现普通人的识谎能力如何？

optionsCn.C: 取决于他们的精神警觉度。
optionsCn.D: 取决于他们的分析能力。

questions.stem: What advice does the new research offer regarding lie detection?

options.A: Looking the speaker in the eye.
options.B: Listening carefully to the speaker.
options.C: Measuring the speaker's breathing rate.
options.D: Focusing on the speaker's facial expressions.

questions.cn: 关于识别谎言，这项新研究提出了什么建议？

optionsCn.C: 测量说话者的呼吸频率。
optionsCn.D: 关注说话者的面部表情。

lines.t: Passage 2.
lines.cn: 短文二。

lines.t: A recent study overturned what we think we know about lying.
lines.cn: 一项近期研究推翻了我们对说谎的既有认知。

lines.t: Most of us have a theory about how to tell if someone is telling a lie.
lines.cn: 我们大多都有一套判断别人是否在说谎的理论。

lines.t: We may develop that theory from observations of those people we know well and see regularly.
lines.cn: 这套理论可能来自我们对那些熟悉且常见的人的观察。

lines.t: But we tend to generalize what we gather from that unscientific daily research and make it a universal theory.
lines.cn: 但我们往往把这种不科学的日常观察所得加以概括，把它变成一套普适理论。

lines.t: So, we might imagine that liars have evasive eyes or the opposite, they simply stare at you.
lines.cn: 于是我们可能以为，说谎的人眼神躲闪，或者相反——直勾勾地盯着你。

lines.t: Or perhaps it is more generally nervous behavior we associate with lies.
lines.cn: 又或者，我们认为与说谎相关的更普遍表现是紧张的行为。

lines.t: Whatever the particular theory, it is usually based on close observation of people we know.
lines.cn: 无论具体是哪套理论，它通常都基于对我们熟悉的人的细致观察。

lines.t: And we get lots of practice.
lines.cn: 而且我们练习的机会很多。

lines.t: On average, we are lied to some 200 times per day.
lines.cn: 平均而言，我们每天会被骗大约 200 次。

lines.t: These are mostly harmless lies, but lies nonetheless.
lines.cn: 这些大多是无害的谎言，但仍是谎言。

lines.t: But there is a problem with our theories, even though they are based on all this observation.
lines.cn: 但尽管这些理论建立在这么多观察之上，它们仍存在问题。

lines.t: The average person, you and me, tested rigorously on how well we detect lies, fails to do better than chance.
lines.cn: 对普通人——也就是你我——进行的严格测试显示，我们识别谎言的能力并不比碰运气更好。

lines.t: That's well established over many studies and lots of attempts by researchers to work out reliable ways to detect lies.
lines.cn: 这一点在大量研究中已得到充分证实，研究者做了许多尝试，想找出可靠的识谎方法。

lines.t: It's even relatively easy to fool lie detectors.
lines.cn: 甚至连测谎仪也相对容易被骗过。

lines.t: The gold standard of lie detection by training yourself in breathing techniques and symptom suppression.
lines.cn: 识谎的黄金标准是训练自己控制呼吸、抑制症状。

lines.t: Is there any way to get better at detecting lies?
lines.cn: 有没有办法提高识谎能力？

lines.t: The new research offers some surprising advice.
lines.cn: 这项新研究提供了一些出人意料的建议。

lines.t: Stop looking and listen instead.
lines.cn: 别再看，改为听。

lines.t: It turns out that if we're unable to see the face, but rather focus on the voice of the person in question, our accuracy rate improves considerably.
lines.cn: 结果表明，如果我们看不到对方的脸，而是专注于其声音，我们的准确率会显著提高。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about most American hospitals?

optionsCn.B: 强烈表示希望被咨询或被告知。
optionsCn.C: 不要说任何听起来负面的话。
optionsCn.D: 把所有医生和护士的名字记下来。

questions.stem: What do American doctors expect their patients to be, according to Karen Brudney?

options.A: Cooperative.
options.B: Appreciative.
options.C: Passive.
options.D: Responsive.

questions.cn: 根据卡伦·布鲁德尼，美国医生期望病人是什么样的？

optionsCn.C: 被动的。
optionsCn.D: 有回应的。

lines.t: Recording 1.
lines.cn: 录音一。

lines.t: Appear to be submissive, humble, grateful and undemanding.
lines.cn: 要显得顺从、谦卑、感恩、不提要求。

lines.t: Show great pleasure when a doctor comes into your room, even if the visit is brief and useless.
lines.cn: 医生走进你的病房时，要表现得非常高兴，哪怕这次查房简短又没什么用。

lines.t: Don't challenge anyone with authority unless you're famous or very rich.
lines.cn: 别去挑战任何有权威的人，除非你很有名或者很有钱。

lines.t: Those are a few strategies for dealing with today's American medical establishment.
lines.cn: 这些就是应对当今美国医疗体制的几条策略。

lines.t: What patients want is to be treated with respect and consideration.
lines.cn: 病人想要的是被尊重、被体谅地对待。

lines.t: But in my experience, too few hospitals and doctors are ready to do that.
lines.cn: 但以我的经验，愿意这么做的医院和医生太少了。

lines.t: In his book, A Whole New Life, novelist Reynolds Price recalls that his doctors chose a crowded hallway as the place to tell him he might have a tumour on his spinal cord.
lines.cn: 小说家雷诺兹·普赖斯在《全新的生活》一书中回忆说，他的医生选择在拥挤的走廊上告诉他，他的脊髓上可能长了肿瘤。

lines.t: It did not occur to the two physicians that a hallway was not the most appropriate place for that particular piece of news.
lines.cn: 那两位医生没想到，走廊并不是宣布这一消息的最合适场所。

lines.t: My surgeon, who is in his mid-thirties, looks tired.
lines.cn: 给我做手术的外科医生三十五六岁，看起来很疲惫。

lines.t: He has been overwhelmed with patients who have fallen on the winter ice.
lines.cn: 他被冬天在冰上摔倒的病人压得喘不过气。

lines.t: He is a witty man, but sometimes his wit is unwelcome.
lines.cn: 他是个机敏的人，但有时他的机敏并不受欢迎。

lines.t: The health insurance company Blue Cross wants me to put you out in the snow tomorrow afternoon, he tells me, after I have been in the hospital for more than a week.
lines.cn: 我住院一个多星期后，他告诉我：“医疗保险公司的蓝十字要求我明天下午把你弄到雪地里去。”

lines.t: I'm terrified because I have no idea where to go.
lines.cn: 我吓坏了，因为我不知道该去哪里。

lines.t: I cannot walk or even lift my leg a few inches.
lines.cn: 我走不了路，连把腿抬起几英寸都做不到。

lines.t: The hospital social worker strikes me as an idiot, but my complaints about her only annoy my surgeon.
lines.cn: 医院的社工在我看来就是个白痴，但我对她的抱怨只会让我的外科医生恼火。

lines.t: I have to work with these people, he tells my friend, Dr.
lines.cn: 他对我的朋友卡伦·布鲁德尼医生说：“我得和这些人共事。”

lines.t: Karen Brudney, when she mercifully intervenes on my behalf and arranges for me to be transferred to another hospital.
lines.cn: 当时布鲁德尼医生好心替我出面，安排我转到了另一家医院。

lines.t: If you say one negative thing, they get defensive, she tells me later.
lines.cn: 她后来告诉我：“你只要说一句负面的意见，他们就会变得防备。”

lines.t: They have this kind of institutional loyalty.
lines.cn: 他们有一种机构性的忠诚。

lines.t: Always bring an advocate, that is, any other person, with you to the hospital, and write down every single question and the answer, the name of every doctor and nurse.
lines.cn: 去医院时一定要带上一个代理人，也就是另一个人，并把每一个问题和答案、每一位医生和护士的姓名都记下来。

lines.t: When people know you have their names, they behave better.
lines.cn: 当人们知道你知道他们的名字时，他们就会表现得更好。

lines.t: And, Brudney adds, if you, as a patient, suggest that you might like to control even part of the situation, or be consulted or informed, then you are considered difficult.
lines.cn: 布鲁德尼还补充说，如果作为病人，你暗示自己哪怕想掌控一部分情况，或者希望被咨询、被告知，那你就会被视为难缠。

lines.t: They want you to be totally passive.
lines.cn: 他们希望你完全被动。

lines.t: The entire healthcare system, particularly hospitals and nursing homes, exists for reasons that have nothing to do with taking care of patients.
lines.cn: 整个医疗体系，尤其是医院和养老院，其存在的理由与照顾病人毫无关系。

lines.t: Patients are incidental.
lines.cn: 病人只是附带之物。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about a team with vitality?

options.A: Its members work together despite risks of failure.
options.B: It prioritizes recruiting young energetic members.
options.C: Its members stay in touch even after it breaks up.
options.D: It grows more and more mature professionally.

questions.cn: 关于一个有活力的团队，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 其成员冒着失败的风险仍然合作。
optionsCn.B: 它优先招募有活力的年轻成员。
optionsCn.C: 其成员在团队解散后仍保持联系。
optionsCn.D: 它在专业上越来越成熟。

questions.stem: What do the researchers find out about members of a team?

options.A: Their differences are likely to impact productivity.
options.B: Their similarity is conducive to future collaboration.
options.C: Their connections strengthen with the passage of time.
options.D: Their mutual understanding stems from a common goal.

questions.cn: 关于团队成员，研究者发现了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们的差异可能影响生产力。
optionsCn.B: 他们的相似性有利于未来的合作。
optionsCn.C: 他们的联系随时间推移而增强。
optionsCn.D: 他们的相互理解源自共同目标。

questions.stem: What do we learn about the team the speaker is currently working in?

options.A: It is characterized by diversity.
options.B: Its goals are quite inconsistent.
options.C: Its members have similar backgrounds.
options.D: It is connected by a unique mechanism.

questions.cn: 关于讲话者目前所在的团队，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.C: 它的成员背景相似。
optionsCn.D: 它通过一种独特机制联系起来。

lines.t: Recording 2.
lines.cn: 录音二。

lines.t: There are probably teams you've worked with that you never want to work with again.
lines.cn: 大概有些你合作过的团队，你再也不想和它们共事了。

lines.t: But there must have also been other teams that you would prize reuniting with professionally.
lines.cn: 但一定也有另一些团队，你会珍视与它们在职业上重逢。

lines.t: In other words, your team had vitality.
lines.cn: 换句话说，你的团队有活力。

lines.t: Vitality comes about when the ties people form with their fellow team members are such that they stay connected even after the team breaks up.
lines.cn: 当人们与团队成员之间建立的纽带使他们在团队解散后仍保持联系时，活力就产生了。

lines.t: What characteristics of a team make its members more likely to stay in contact despite no longer working together?
lines.cn: 一个团队具备什么特征，会让其成员即使不再共事也更可能保持联系？

lines.t: This question has been answered recently in a study published in a business journal.
lines.cn: 这个问题最近在一项发表于商业期刊的研究中得到了回答。

lines.t: One of the two key factors the research team discovered is sameness, specifically sharing the same gender or ethnic origin.
lines.cn: 研究团队发现的两个关键因素之一是相似性，具体指同性别或同族裔。

lines.t: The more members of a team share similar demographics, the more inclined they'll be to remain associates long after the team has served its purpose.
lines.cn: 团队成员在人口特征上越相似，他们在团队使命完成很久之后仍保持同事关系的倾向就越强。

lines.t: After ties are established, similarity strengthens them.
lines.cn: 纽带建立之后，相似性会强化它们。

lines.t: As a result, they regard these individuals with greater trust and mutual understanding, which motivates them to seek further opportunities for collaboration.
lines.cn: 结果，他们对这些人抱有更大的信任和相互理解，这促使他们寻求进一步的合作机会。

lines.t: In effect, people tend to create stronger and longer-lasting connections with similar others.
lines.cn: 实际上，人们往往与和自己相似的人建立更牢固、更持久的联系。

lines.t: Someone who looks and sounds different from us may have the resources we need to be more successful, yet we find them to be significantly less credible simply because they are different.
lines.cn: 一个与我们外貌和口音都不同的人，可能拥有我们需要以取得更大成功的资源，但我们却仅仅因为对方不同，就认为他们可信度低得多。

lines.t: If you are a fierce advocate of workplace diversity, you'll no doubt be horrified by such a revelation.
lines.cn: 如果你热烈主张职场多元化，这个发现无疑会让你震惊。

lines.t: The second factor identified by the researchers is the quality of the relationships among the team members.
lines.cn: 研究者指出的第二个因素是团队成员之间关系的质量。

lines.t: The more they trust one another, share the same goals, and depend on each other for the achievement of those goals, the stronger their chances of maintaining their connections despite no longer working as one team.
lines.cn: 他们越信任彼此、目标一致、并在实现这些目标上相互依赖，即使不再作为一个团队共事，保持联系的可能性就越大。

lines.t: Teams with quality relationships have a shared belief that it's safe to take risks with each other, and that members are obliged to share the workload and help out.
lines.cn: 关系质量高的团队有一种共同信念：彼此之间冒风险是安全的，成员有义务分担工作量、互相帮忙。

lines.t: From personal experience, I can see both the truth and the inconsistency of such studies.
lines.cn: 从个人经验看，我既能看到这类研究中的真实，也能看到它的自相矛盾。

lines.t: The truth is some of my closest friendships were formed as a result of having worked together on teams, and I actively seek opportunities to work with them again.
lines.cn: 真实的一面是：我最亲密的一些友谊是在团队共事中形成的，而我会主动寻找与它们再次合作的机会。

lines.t: The inconsistency, though, is that I've never worked for a team more successful and cohesive than the one of which I'm a member right now, and yet the four of us have very little in common and are completely different demographically, so I'm unlikely to question the value of a diverse workforce.
lines.cn: 而矛盾之处在于：我从未与哪个团队共事得比我现在的团队更成功、更团结，然而我们四个人几乎没有共同点，人口特征也完全不同，所以我难以质疑多元化工作队伍的价值。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 3 组
tasks.context: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do experts recommend concerning being thrifty?

options.A: Putting aside twenty percent of one's earnings.
options.B: Spending in anticipation of becoming wealthy.
options.C: Living off a small proportion of one's income.
options.D: Saving as much as one can possibly manage.

questions.cn: 关于节俭，专家建议什么？

optionsCn.B: 指望自己将变富而提前花销。
optionsCn.C: 靠收入的一小部分生活。
optionsCn.D: 尽可能多地存钱。

questions.stem: How does confidence help people to be thrifty?

options.A: It empowers them to cope with irrational emotions.
options.B: It will guarantee the profits from their investments.
options.C: It will turn them into successful financial planners.
options.D: It enables them to focus on long-term investments.

questions.cn: 自信如何帮助人们保持节俭？

optionsCn.A: 它使他们能够应对非理性的情绪。
optionsCn.B: 它能保证他们投资的收益。
optionsCn.C: 它会让他们成为成功的理财规划师。
optionsCn.D: 它使他们能够专注于长期投资。

questions.stem: How do millionaires react when they fail in their investment?

options.A: They count on others to take the responsibility.
options.B: They change their investment strategy in time.
options.C: They think they themselves are to blame.
options.D: They persist rather than get discouraged.

questions.cn: 投资失败时，百万富翁如何反应？

optionsCn.A: 他们指望别人承担责任。
optionsCn.B: 他们及时改变投资策略。
optionsCn.C: 他们认为该怪自己。
optionsCn.D: 他们坚持而不气馁。

questions.stem: Why does the speaker say millionaires are socially indifferent? That's the end of Listening Comprehension.

options.A: They do not resist novel lifestyles.
options.B: They do not try to keep up with others.
options.C: They do not care what they have acquired.
options.D: They do not pressure themselves to get rich.

questions.cn: 讲话者为什么说百万富翁对社交淡漠？

optionsCn.A: 他们不抵制新奇的生活方式。
optionsCn.B: 他们不试图与别人攀比。
optionsCn.C: 他们不在乎自己所拥有的东西。
optionsCn.D: 他们不给自己施加致富的压力。

lines.t: Recording 3.
lines.cn: 录音三。

lines.t: An American researcher who studied 600 millionaires found how rich you can get comes down to six wealth factors.
lines.cn: 一位研究过 600 位百万富翁的美国研究者发现，你能变多富取决于六项财富因素。

lines.t: She found that six behaviors are related to net worth potential.
lines.cn: 她发现，有六种行为与净值潜力相关。

lines.t: Regardless of age or income, these were thriftiness, confidence, responsibility, planning, focus, and social indifference.
lines.cn: 无论年龄或收入如何，这六项是：节俭、自信、责任感、计划性、专注和对社交的淡漠。

lines.t: Being thrifty comes as no great surprise.
lines.cn: 节俭并不令人意外。

lines.t: Spending above your means, spending instead of saving for retirement, spending in anticipation of becoming wealthy, makes you a slave to the paycheck.
lines.cn: 超支消费、不存钱为退休准备、指望自己将变富而提前花销，都会让你成为薪水的奴隶。

lines.t: Even with an astronomical level of income, she wrote, to properly build wealth, experts recommend saving 20% of your income and living off the remaining 80%.
lines.cn: 她写道，即便收入高得惊人，要正确积累财富，专家建议存下收入的 20%，靠剩下的 80% 生活。

lines.t: Having confidence is another key characteristic, as it helps people to be thrifty.
lines.cn: 自信是另一个关键特征，因为它有助于人们保持节俭。

lines.t: It takes confidence to live within your means.
lines.cn: 量入为出需要自信。

lines.t: It also takes confidence to invest properly.
lines.cn: 正确投资也需要自信。

lines.t: Instead of making investing decisions with your emotions, financial planners advise that you should leave your investments alone and focus on a long-term investment plan.
lines.cn: 理财规划师建议，不要凭情绪做投资决策，而应让投资保持不动，专注于长期投资计划。

lines.t: But people can't invest, or manage their own money, without accepting responsibility for the outcomes.
lines.cn: 但人们若不接受结果的责任，就无法投资或管理好自己的钱。

lines.t: Many millionaires take on personal responsibility, and most also happen to be self-made, meaning they didn't acquire their wealth through luck.
lines.cn: 许多百万富翁承担个人责任，而且大多数恰好是白手起家，也就是说他们并非靠运气获得财富。

lines.t: Millionaires don't count on anyone else to make them rich, and they don't blame anyone else if they fall short.
lines.cn: 百万富翁不指望别人让他们变富，如果没做到也不怪别人。

lines.t: They focus on things they can control, and align their daily habits to the goals they have set for themselves.
lines.cn: 他们专注于自己能掌控的事情，并让自己的日常习惯与自己设定的目标保持一致。

lines.t: They tend to be goal-oriented and hard workers, which enables them to plan financially and focus on seeing those plans through.
lines.cn: 他们往往目标明确、勤奋工作，这使他们能够做财务规划，并专注于把规划贯彻到底。

lines.t: 92% of millionaires surveyed developed a long-term plan for their money, and 97% almost always achieved the goals they set for themselves.
lines.cn: 受访的百万富翁中，92% 为自己的钱制定了长期计划，97% 几乎总能实现自己设定的目标。

lines.t: And it is these behaviors that make it easy for them to be socially indifferent.
lines.cn: 正是这些行为让他们能够轻易做到对社交的淡漠。

lines.t: They resist lifestyle creep, the tendency to spend more whenever one earns more.
lines.cn: 他们抵制“生活方式升级”——即收入一增加就想多花钱的倾向。

lines.t: Essentially, they don't yield to pressure to buy the latest thing or to keep up with others, or what they have acquired.
lines.cn: 本质上，他们不会屈服于购买最新款、与人攀比或炫耀所得的压力。

lines.t: Instead of being focused on what might make them happy today, they're focused on their long-term wealth-building plan.
lines.cn: 他们关注的不是什么能让自己当下快乐，而是自己的长期财富积累计划。
